body.label: Folio 5r (second section)
body.value:
1. המה ובמצרים מצאתים מאשר היו לבלעם בן בעור ואני
  2. מרפא בהם את החולים. ויאמרו לו אנו נדע כי אתה
  3. משוטט בעולם וגם אתה עושה מעשים רעים ואתה
  4. חוטא ואתה תתעה את אנשי העולם בספר קאלה. ספר לנו
  5. באמת ואם לא נהרוג אותך. ויאמר להם אתם {אנ} אדוני ואני
  6. אומר לכם אמת. דעו כי הספרים האלה המה ליוחנן 
  7. הצובע אשר למדתי ממנו. ענה פטלוס השר ויאמר
  8. לרבי יהושע בן פרחיה הנשיא וגם למרינוס זקן {שליהודה}
  9. שליהודים מאי זה מקום הוא זה יוח{ש֯}<נ>ן הצובע השיבו
  10. אתו ויאמרו לו באמת דבר לנו ישוע הרשע כי הספ<ר>ים
  11. האלה של יוחנן הצובע המה. וישוע הרשע זה לא הוא
  12. כתובם כי אם יוחנן הצובע ויהיו חוטאים בהם וגם היו
  13. מתעים את אנשי העולם. ויענו {=} רבותינו ויאמהו לפטלוס
  14. אם ירצה אדונינו רשות שנהרוג את הרש{ר}עים האלה
  15. שהם מתעסקים בכשפים ובכתבים <ש>לאון. והמה מתעים
  16. בני אדם ואומרים להם יש בידינו להמית וגם להחיות.
  17. ויחיבו את נפשותם להריגה והם מחשבים שהם שותפים
  18. לאלוה. אבי ר<א>ה נא מה עשו אלה האנשים קמו ויתעו לאנשים
  19. הרבה ויובילו אתם אל המדבר ועתה ימותו מן הרעב וגם
  20. הכסף אשר עלי<ה>ם חק לתת לאדונינו לא יעזבום שיתנו.
  21. ויכתוב פטלוס השר ויאמר להם אם ארצו גם אני אשלח
  22. עליהם וגם אביא את יוחנן הצובע. ונראה מה יצא מן
  23. {המפש} המשפט ונשפוט עליהם. ויענו אתו ו<י>אמרו לו
  24. הן שלח את יהודה הלובש קרועים וגם את שמעון כופא
  25. ואת בנימין המקולל בגיס. וישלח אותם את אלה וילכו אל
  26. כפר נחום המדינה וימצאו את יוחנן והוא אסור בבית הכלא.
  27. בעבור כי אסרו טברינוס קיסר שהיה מתעה לאנשי עולם.
  28. ויביאו את יוחנן הצובע מלמד שישוע הרשע לפני
  29. יהושע בן פרחיה הנשיא ולפני מרינוס זקן <ש>ליהוד<י>ם ולפני
  30. פטלוס השר. ויענו ויאמרו אלה הספרים אשר מצאנו
  31. ביד ישוע הרשע תלמידך,  {ב֯} אם תאמר לנו באמת
  32. נעזבך ואם לא נהרוג אותך בחרב פיפיות. השיב יוחנן

body.value:
1. and I found them in Egypt, from those that belonged to Balaam son of Beor, and I
  2. heal the sick with them.” They said to him: “We know that you
  3. roam the world, and you also do evil deeds, and you
  4. sin and also mislead the people of the world with these books. Tell us
  5. the truth, and if not— we will kill you.” He said to them: “You are my masters and I 
  6. say to you (the) truth. Know that these books are by Yoḥanan
  7. the Dyer, from whom I have learned.” Petalus the governor answered and said
  8. to Rabbi Yehoshuʿa ben Peraḥiah the Nasi, and also to Marinus, the elder
  9. of the Jews: “From which place is this Yoḥanan the Dyer?” They answered
  10. him and said to him: “In truth did Yeshuʿa the wicked say to us that these books
  11. belong to Yoḥanan the Dyer, and this wicked Yeshuʿa did not
  12. write them, but Yoḥanan the Dyer (did). And they sinned with them, and they also
  13. misled the people of the world.” And our rabbis answered and said to Petalus:
  14. “If our master wishes authority, that we will kill these
  15. wicked men, since they are dealing with magic and with writings of falsehood, and they mislead
  16. people and say to them, ‘We have (the ability) to kill and also to revive’,
  17. and they make their souls liable to being killed. And they think that they are equal with God.
  18. Father, please see what these people have done—they rose and misled many people,
  19. and led them to the desert, and now they will die of hunger; and also
  20. the money which is with them—it is the law to give it to our master, (but) they will not let them give it.”
  21. And Petalus the governor wrote and said to them: “If you wish, I too will send
  22. for them, and will also bring Yoḥanan the Dyer, and we shall see what comes out of
  23. the trial, and we will try them.” They answered him and said to him (i.e., Pilatus):
  24. “Yes; send Yehudah, who wears torn (garments), and also Shimeʿon Kepha,
  25. and Binyamin who is cursed in the army (?). He sent them, these (men), and they went to
  26. the town Kephar Naḥum, and found Yoḥanan imprisoned in jail,
  27. for Tiberinus Caesar had imprisoned him, since he had been misleading the people of the world.
  28. And they brought Yoḥanan the Dyer, the teacher of Yeshuʿa the wicked, before
  29. Yehoshuʿa ben Peraḥiah the Nasi and before Marinus the elder of the Jews, and before
  30. Petalus the governor. They answered and said: “These books that we found
  31. the hand of Yeshuʿa the wicked, your disciple—if you tell us in truth
  32. we will release you, but if not, we will kill you by a double-edged sword.” Yoḥanan answered

body.value:
1. and said to them: “My masters! These books are books of magicians, and Yeshuʿa
  2. the wicked wrote (them), and I was in jail, since Tiberinus Caesar
  3. had imprisoned me. And I did not see Yeshuʿa the wicked, but he and his eleven
  4. disciples wrote these books, and they are dealing with them
  5. and mislead (the) people of the world. And they say about me that they (i.e., the books) are mine,
  6. but he wrote them out of his own mind.” Then they said to Yoḥanan the Dyer that:
  7. “The disciples of Yeshuʿa the wicked—what are their names?” Yoḥanan answered and said: “These are
  8. their names—Naqi and Alqi and Zakai, Teini and Todah and Patros and Netzer and Situ. These are
  9. their names.” They said to him: “Who will go and bring them to us?”
  10. And Yehudah who wears the torn (garments) said to them, with Shimeʿon Kepha and with Binyamin the curse
  11. of the army (?). And they summoned them, and said: “Will you go and bring them?” And they said: “We will go.”
  12. They went and came to the town of Kephar Naḥum and were wandering after them, and they (i.e., the disciples) heard
  13. and ran away to the town Africa, and hid under a certain tree, and they were dealing
  14. with magic, which they learned from Yeshuʿa the wicked, and they were under the roots of the tree.
  15. And Satai, and Altagius, and Alqi and Paulus and Petrus and Zakai ran away from them.
  16. And those who remained—they brought them before Rabbi Yehoshuʿa ben Peraḥiah the Nasi,
  17. and before Marinus the elder of the Jews, and before Petalus, and before the
  18. crowd of people. And they (R. Yehoshuʿa ben Peraḥiah et al.) saw them; and he was standing—Yeshuʿa the wicked; 
  19. and Yoḥanan the Dyer was also standing. They said to Naqi: “Why
  20. is your name called Naqi?” He answered them and said to them: “About me David said, ‘Neqi hands
  21. and a pure heart’.” They answered him and said to him: “You are light(-minded) and a fool who misled (?)
  22. yourself from all living creature! Not thus said David about you, but in the Torah
  23. it is written thus, ‘and He shall naqe not yenaqe’.” And they ordered about him and threw him into
  24. a fiery furnace. And after him they summoned Matai, and said to him: “Why is
  25. your name called Matai?” He answered and said to them: “About me David said, ‘Matai will I come and be seen
  26. before God?’” They answered him and said to him: “You are (more) light(-minded) and a fool than all living creatures!
  27. Not thus said David about you (in) the Bible, for it says afterwards, ‘Matai will he die,
  28. and his name perish’” And they ordered about him, and they cut Matai’s head off from his body.
  29. After him they summoned Beni, and they said to him: “Why is your name called
  30. Beni?” He said to them: “About me the Bible says in the Torah, ‘Israel is beni, the firstborn’.”
  31. And they answered him and said to him: “You are light(-minded) and a fool of all living creatures! Not thus did it speak

  2. And it was decreed upon him, and they burned him in the fire, and Beni died in the fire.
  3. Afterwards they summoned Netzer, and they said to him: “Why is your name called Netzer?” And he said to them: “About me the
  4. prophet Isaiah prophesied, as it is written, ‘and a netzer will grow from its roots’.” And they answered and said
  5. to him: “You are (more) light(-minded) and a fool than all living creatures for speaking thus! Not thus did
  6. Isaiah speak about you, but thus—‘And you were cast out of your tomb
  7. like a detested netzer’.” And they ordered concerning him, and they stoned him—Netzer—with a stone.
  8. Then they summoned Todah, and they said to him: “Why did they call your name Todah?” He said to them:
  9. “For this (reason) they called me Todah, for about me David said, ‘Come to His gates with todah (=thanksgiving)’.”
  10. They answered him and said to him: “You are light(-minded) and a fool of all living creatures!
  11. For Scripture did not speak about you, and not thus did David speak; rather, it is written
  12. in the Torah, ‘And when you sacrifice a sacrifice of todah (=thanksgiving)’. And David too said, ‘He who sacrifices todah
  13. honors me’.” And they ordered upon him, and they executed Todah. After this Petalus the governor said
  14. to Rabbi Yehoshuʿa ben Peraḥiah the Nasi and to Marinus the elder

  9. ויען טברינוס המלך ויאמר ליהודים אשריכם כי אלהיכם גלה
  10. לכם את הרזים. ויבלבל את עצת אלה המכשפים {ה}
  11. המרגיזים לפניו בכל יום. השיבו וענו רבותינו אותו
  12. ואמרו לטברינוס המלך מה חייב מן הדין אשר נשפוט {להם}
  13. אותם. ויענ[ה] ויאמר להם עשו להם כאשר תחפוצו שלא
  14. יאבדו אתכם מן העולם. בעת ההיא אמרו  <את> שניהם ושלח
  15. אותם אל טבריא אשר ביהוד המדינה. ויציב להם עץ
  16. ויתלו אותם את יוחנן הצובע מלמד ישוע הרשע וימת֯
  17. ויקברו אתו. ואחריו העלו את ישוע הרשע אל העץ
  18. [    י]דע כ֯י֯ כ֯ת֯וב לנו לא תלין נבלתו על העץ. אמר
  19. [           לא]נ֯ש֯ים היו֯ מאמינים בו אם תבואו
  20. למ֯ח֯ר֯ ולא תראו֯[ני ולא] ג֯ופי על הע֯ץ֯ ד֯עו כי עליתי לשמיא
  21. ו֯כ֯ן נודע לנו כי כאש֯ר֯ תלו על העץ הוא הי֯ה֯ מתעה
  22. בכשפים. ויבקש מהם חומץ תקיף וישתה. וירגמוהו
  23. על העץ וימת על העץ. ויורידוהו ויקברוהו תחת צנור
  24. המים בתוך פרדס יהודה הפרדסי. ובבקר ביום אחד֯
  25. בשבת נק<ב>צו בני האדם א{נ}<ש>ר{ם} התעה אותם ישוע {ה}
  26. הרשע ויתפשו את היהודים. ויאמרו להם באמת סַפֵר
  27. לנו ישוע [כ]י היהודים בשקר עסיקים. איה האיש
  28. אשר תליתם באמת לשמים עלה. ויאמר פטלוס השר
  29. ליהודה הפרדסי האיש אשר תלִיתָה אותו גופו מה עשית
  30. בה֯. ענה ויאמר לו כי ישוע הרשע לפני אשר יעלו אותו֯
  31. [א]ל העץ֯ היה קורא לא[נשים א]שר היה מחטיא אותם ויאמר...

body.label: Folio 6v (fifth section)
body.value:
1. and He commanded the angel who is in charge of the house of the child and of the womb, and he shaped the child
  2. and placed and dropped a stone [there?].  And when the Lord confounded their counsel, the people of
  3. the kingdom answered Yeshuʿa the wicked and said to him: “The woman who became pregnant—why
  4. did she not give birth?” He answered and said to them: “There are among the people of the Jews men who
  5. do not let the child leave his mother’s belly alive,
  6. so that you will know, our master the king, that we are both the sons of the God
  7. of Heaven.”  And they took iron tools, and tore up her belly, and extracted from
  8. “the house of the child,” from the womb, a stone. And that virgin died.
  9. King Tiberinus answered and said to the Jews: “Blessed are you, for your God revealed
  10. the mysteries to you, and confounded the counsel of these magicians
  11. who irritate Him every day.” Our teachers answered
  12. and said to King Tiberinus: “What is due by law that we will judge
  13. them?” He answered and said to them: “Do to them as you wish, so that they will not
  14. destroy you from the world.” At that time they shackled both of them and he sent
  15. them to Tiberias which is in the town of Yahud, and he set up a tree for them.
  16. And they hung them—Yoḥanan the Dyer, the teacher of Yeshuʿa the wicked, and he died,
  17. and they buried him. And after him (i.e., Yoḥanan) they raised Yeshuʿa the wicked up to the tree.
  18. [He k]new that it is written for us, “Do not let his corpse remain overnight on the tree.” He said
  19. [ ... ... to the p]eople who believed in him: “If you come
  20. tomorrow and do not see [me nor] my body on the tree—know that I ascended to Heaven.
  21. And we also heard that when they hung (him) on the tree, he was misleading
  22. with magic, and he asked them for powerful vinegar and he drank (it). They stoned him 
  23.  on the tree, and he died on the tree. They brought him down and buried him under the water-
  24. pipe inside the orchard of Yehudah the orchard-man. In the morning of the Sunday, 
  25. the people whom Yeshuʿa the wicked had misled gathered
  26. together, and caught the Jews, and said to them: “In truth Yeshuʿa told
  27. us that the Jews are dealing with a lie; where is the man
  28. whom you hung? In truth, he ascended to Heaven.” Petalus the governor said
  29. to Yehudah the orchard-man: “The man whom you (sg.) have hung—what did you (sg.) do
  30. with his body?” He (i.e., Yehudah) answered and said to him that : “Yeshuʿa the wicked, before he was raised
  31. upon the tree, was  calling the p[eople w]hom he was leading into sin, and said [to them...].”
